names: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
summary: Approximately 1,001 km² and about 204,327 people (2017), from Wikidata's Q1039 (P2046, P1082). The English Wikipedia article "São Tomé and Príncipe", at revision 1375996168, opens: "São Tomé and Príncipe, officially the Democratic Republic of Sao Tome and Principe, is an island country in the Gulf of Guinea, off the western equatorial coast of Central Africa. It consists of two archipelagos around the two main islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, about 81 nautical miles apart and about 135 and 121 nautical miles off the northwestern coast of Gabon. With a population of 201,800, São Tomé and Príncipe is the second-smallest and second-least populous African sovereign state after Seychelles." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Portugal claimed the two islands in the Gulf of Guinea in the 1470s and worked them as sugar and then as cocoa plantations. They became a state on 12 July 1975, the last of the African territories to leave. They are the smallest of the five and the one where the transfer of power met least resistance. Nobody fought a war there, and the single movement Lisbon recognised took the state from an assembly elected four days earlier.
